status: Integrated B1 source-fit design requires actual use of First Nation, Métis and Inuit government response cases plus the previously qualified social/environmental government-and-citizen plans. No learner attainment or real plan implementation is asserted.

nation-response.use: Previously verified NFN/provincial fishery action, purpose, survey evidence and qualified effectiveness.
nation-response.limits: Actual2015–2022 source period; no post2025 renewal, quota advice or effort→population inference.

metis-response.provider: Manitoba Métis Federation, National Government of the Red River Métis
metis-response.use: Describes obtaining supplies/accommodation for displaced citizens and announces a command centre with support; citizens are invited to volunteer or contribute.
metis-response.limits: This is a dated government response account/announcement. It does not independently prove every placement happened, count all evacuees or establish that the emergency ended. No actual donation, enrolment, travel or use of old contact/service instructions.

inuit-response.provider: Nunatsiavut Government, Health and Social Development, Community Programs
inuit-response.reviewed: Complete current main body, including community offices and food-security sections.
inuit-response.use: Describes community/regional programme roles and food-security measures such as community freezers, kitchens and meal-bag programmes.
inuit-response.limits: Undated programme descriptions read2026-11-11; the2014 food-security statistic is not a current prevalence claim. The programme’s existence or its stated intent does not establish elimination of food insecurity or identical provision in every community.

both-action-plans.use: Actual original social and environmental designs, each with explicit appropriate-government and citizen steps, methods, purpose, feasibility/progress limits and changed-case check.

whole-civic-operation.use: Retain actual achieved civic case, shared values and original campaign plan rather than infer whole mastery from a response headline.

whole-inquiry-operation.use: Retain actual evidence patterns, original supported conclusion, conditional prediction and relevant improvement; no formal causal or all-group opinion inference.

first-nation.government: Nipissing First Nation, alongside its distinct provincial partner in the dated case
facts: Council introduced documented fisheries-law measures; staff gathered harvest evidence and worked with provincial staff on assessment.
The joint report records partial recovery with an unmet management goal and important year-to-year/causal limits.
first-nation.assessmentFocus: Relate actual measures and shared roles to the stated concern, and assess the available implementation/result evidence without inventing full recovery.

metis.government: Manitoba Métis Federation, National Government of the Red River Métis
metis.issue: Displacement and immediate needs during May2025 Manitoba wildfires
facts: The government update reports work to obtain supplies and safe accommodation, and announces a command centre for displaced citizens.
It identifies citizen support/volunteer roles alongside the government/community resource response.
metis.assessmentFocus: Explain how supplies/accommodation could address the displacement issue. Distinguish the source’s reported work and announced service from verified completed placements, total need met or an end to wildfire impacts.

inuit.government: Nunatsiavut Government, regional/community Health and Social Development programme
inuit.issue: Food access and associated community well-being needs in the studied Labrador Inuit region
facts: The department describes community offices with locally tailored plans and regional support.
It describes community freezers and food-literacy/kitchen/meal-bag actions as part of a multi-part food-security approach.
inuit.assessmentFocus: Explain the relationship between the stated need and different programme actions; identify what actual outcome evidence would be needed before claiming the issue was solved. Do not generalise a regional description to every Inuit person or community.

learnerSteps.instruction: Use all three original attributed case cards and their actual sources. For each, identify the named government, significant issue, purpose and actual reported/announced response. Explain the intended relationship between action and issue, then assess what available evidence establishes about implementation or effects and what it does not. A stated intention is not a measured outcome; a limited supported assessment is valid. Keep the source dates, regional/people distinctions and government-versus-citizen roles.

Compare the cases without treating them as identical problems or competing success rankings. Show a supported interrelationship, such as distinct Nation/provincial assessment roles, government resources plus citizen support, or regional staff and community-tailored delivery. Use the actual fishery data for a specific scientific evidence pattern; do not force graphs of unrelated programme mentions or compare incomparable outcome units.

Actually produce both previously prepared social and environmental action plans. Each must include appropriate government and citizen steps, explained purpose and role fit, feasible methods/sequence and a bounded way to check progress. Keep actual provider facts distinct from hypothetical proposed actions; choosing two governments alone is not a plan, and a citizen poster is not a measured ecological or social solution.

Communicate an original supported oral/written judgment, give a clearly conditional prediction for a changed supplied response/monitoring situation, and suggest a relevant evidence or method improvement. Keep source-supported observations distinct from unsupported causation, a group-wide viewpoint or a desired political conclusion.

Retain the complete prior Ontario local-governance case/entity checks and the complete civic shared-goal/achieved-case/original-plan operation. Apply the response-assessment and actor/method reasoning to a changed supplied issue, identifying an unknown responsibility fact rather than assigning a nearby city automatically. These source-component tasks do not infer complete national/Indigenous structure knowledge or any child’s whole topic mastery.

integrated-responses-and-plans.positive: Assesses actual source-bounded responses of all three named Indigenous government kinds, relates actions/purposes/evidence/limits, and develops both government-and-citizen social/environmental plans using the qualified prior specifics.
nearMiss: Uses only one First Nation case and calls all Indigenous government requirements complete.
Treats an announcement, programme listing or volunteer invitation as proof all needs were met.
Produces only government actions or only citizen actions, or only one social/environmental plan.
Treats all governments or Indigenous peoples as interchangeable, or gives an unsupported political judgment instead of source-based response assessment.

wholeClaimLimits: Existing cards/guides/intervals/edges remain exact. Ontario-governance contributes the actual studied Ontario authority operation; additional supplied government response facts do not silently broaden that claim or certify all current B3.3 institutions. Shared inquiry/civic operations retain their whole checks. Source-fit authoring is not a classroom trial or learner mastery.
